  • In the provided corpus, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, setup.py execution, abused PEP 517 build hooks, or malicious import-time side effects.
  • entry_points.txt exists in the manifest, but its contents were not provided. The README describes the aether CLI and python -m aether.mcp as user-invoked entry points.
  • The README describes Claude Code plugin SessionStart/Stop hooks, but these appear to be documented plugin behavior after a user runs claude plugin install ...; this is not evidence of malicious automatic execution during PyPI package installation or Python interpreter startup.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Exfiltration/staging: no evidence of archive staging, temporary harvesting, webhook upload, suspicious C2, or raw IP upload.
  • Persistence: no evidence of systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile edits, or self-reinstall/background persistence loops. ~/.aether/mcp_state.json appears to be documented application state storage.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence of Kubernetes service-account use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions/token theft, registry token reuse, or workflow injection.
  • Obfuscation/loaders: pre-scan hits on re.compile and README text such as “depl…” appear to be benign text-analysis regexes/documentation, not base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec staged loader behavior.
